key_insight: A nonconforming reduced enriched quartic finite element can solve the surface biharmonic problem using only vertex values and scalar edge moments, avoiding both stabilization and Piola transforms.
engineering_relevance: This gives a simpler, standard-assembly FEM for higher-order PDEs on curved surfaces with provable stability and convergence on sufficiently refined meshes.
method: Uses a reduced enriched quartic (REQ) element with vertex values and edge moments only.
Applies the same local triangle construction on every piecewise planar surface element.
Proves weak discrete Miranda–Talenti-type estimates to ensure uniform stability and error control.
evidence_signal: The paper reports numerical tests on three surfaces, confirming the predicted convergence rates and examining discrete Miranda–Talenti constants and angle-defect scaling.
watch_item: The method’s stability is guaranteed only on sufficiently refined interpolating surface meshes, so mesh quality and refinement level matter in practice.
paper_title: A Finite Element Method for the Surface Biharmonic Problem without Stabilization or Piola Transforms
